messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Region-westus2 Private DNS propagation delays detected for Azure private zones used by Redwood Private deployments. A subset of customer queries are resolving to stale on-prem IPs; increased packet loss observed. Auto-page: @oncall-azure, @jamie-sre

sara.ops: seeing elevated 5xx from a few private clusters, started a quick smoke check. customers on dedicated VPNs showing ~25-40% request failures to model endpoints.

jamie-sre: confirmed. Traceroutes from our edge -> westus2 show flapping where some DNS answers return old CNAMEs/IPs that route to on-prem. Looks like private DNS replication lag between zone masters and forwarders.

lee-net: adding context — the affected customers are using Azure Private DNS with conditional forwarders to their on-prem resolvers via VPN gateway. If Azure answers stale records the on-prem networks send traffic back into an old path that no longer handles traffic, so packets drop.

chris-support: customer impact list: two mid-market customers (acct:redwood-acct-331, acct:boxwave) report slow/error model responses and timeouts. Support escalated to P1 and notified customers.

maya-eng: can we confirm whether this is a control-plane DNS replication issue on Azure side vs. our config? I can run a query sweep from multiple points.

oncall-azure: I'm on it. I've opened a ticket with Azure NOC (ref: 2310-az-wus2-dns-prop). They're seeing elevated Private DNS update latency in the region — suspected internal service scheduler backlog after a config push. They say they have a mitigation plan to force-resync zone masters. ETA for resync ~ 12-15 mins.

jamie-sre: immediate mitigation plan: 1) Reduce TTLs to 30s is too late. Instead we should enforce local resolver overrides in our Private control plane for impacted customers to point to healthy fallback IPs in westus3 (same cluster replica). 2) Temporarily reroute traffic via our routing policy to prefer cross-region replica. 3) Notify customers about planned temporary failover if we execute. Thoughts?

sara.ops: +1 to routing policy override. We need a quick canary for one customer before broad switch. Who can deploy the route override?

lee-net: I can push policy change. Will create an override route for acct:redwood-acct-331 first. Command (internal CLI):

```
redwood route override --customer acct:redwood-acct-331 --from-region westus2 --to-region westus3 --type dns-redirect --ttl 60
```

I'll roll that to one cluster now.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: redwood-route-override/2026-03-15T03:21Z by lee-net.

jamie-sre: good. After canary if stable for 3m, roll to boxwave then to remaining affected. Also update rate-limit and cache bust policies so we don't cause cache stampedes.

chris-support: I'll update customer comms: short note that we're failing over to an alternate region due to Azure Private DNS propagation delays; no config changes required from them. ETA 20m.

maya-eng: running verification probes now: querying private zone from edge, westus2 app nodes, on-prem forwarder endpoints. Logging to internal gist. Early results: canary route shows 15% error -> after override dropped to 2% within 90s.

oncall-azure: Azure NOC reports resync started, but propagation will be staggered across forwarders. Keep failover until we see consistent correct answers from all forwarders.

lee-net: rolling to boxwave now. Running the override pushes with a 30s stagger.

incident-bot: NOTE: on-call handoff scheduled in 30m. Current oncall: @oncall-azure until 04:00Z. Handoff to @jamie-sre if still active.

jamie-sre: checklist to close incident: 1) Azure confirms all forwarders returning expected records for private zones 2) Our probes stable <1% errors for 15m 3) Remove temporary overrides and monitor for 5m 4) Postmortem owner assigned.

chris-support: customers acknowledged and fine with temporary region failover. Ticket updates posted.

maya-eng: probes show full recovery in 12m; Azure NOC confirms resync complete. I'll remove canary override and watch.

lee-net: removing overrides now (reverting to normal DNS). Command: `redwood route override --remove --customer acct:redwood-acct-331 --id r-2026-321`

deploy-bot: deploy completed: redwood-route-override/2026-03-15T03:30Z by lee-net.

jamie-sre: monitoring. No spike in errors after rollback.

chris-support: informing customers that normal routing restored and Azure confirmed internal fix. They're asking for RCA and timeline.

sara.ops: assigning postmortem: jamie-sre owner, lee-net support, maya-eng data. Postmortem to include: timeline, root cause (Azure private DNS scheduler backlog + zone resync lag), impact list, mitigation steps we took (regional failover overrides), and suggested product changes (improve automatic cross-region fallback, add probe-based automatic failover for private clusters).

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: region-westus2-private-dns-stale-prop - severity: P1 -> downgraded to P3 after mitigation. Closing thread in 2h for postmortem consolidation. :white_check_mark:
